newsitem.title: INDIA: Marxists celebrate 20 years' rule in Indian state.
newsitem.headline: Marxists celebrate 20 years' rule in Indian state.

text.p: India's Marxist chief of the eastern state of West Bengal, which is celebrating 20 years of uninterrupted communist rule, pledged on Friday to step up efforts to attract foreign private investment.
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) CPI (M) rode to power in 1977 but announced a radical market-friendly investment programme only in 1994.

"We are moving with a target of attracting investment to the tune of hundreds of billion of rupees in the next ten years," Jyoti Basu, the 82-year-old soft-spoken chief minister of West Bengal, told reporters in the eastern city of Calcutta.

West Bengal attracted investment worth 102.69 billion rupees ($2.87 billion) in 1995 against 21.89 billion in the previous year. Foreign investment, including those by non-resident Indians, approved in 1995 stood at 31.52 billion rupees compared with 9.41 billion in 1994.
Investment approvals in the first ten months of 1996 stood at 62.25 billion rupees.
Basu said there was no place for complacency even though his government had achieved considerable success in rural development.
The CPI (M)'s stay in power for two decades is mainly attributed to the radical reforms introduced in the agricultural sector.
The communist government launched a radical land re-distribution programme and held elections to the local village level government soon after it assumed office in 1977.

"We are first among many Indian states in a number of areas. We shall not remain backward in the field of industry and we have to match other developed states in foreign and private investments," he said.
Basu said that despite great success in land reforms, hundreds of acres of land could not be distributed among the sharecroppers due to litigation in courts.
"We have to do a little better for improving the situation," he said.

The number of sharecroppers who were given land rights through land reforms numbered about two million and over a million acres of land was re-distributed to the landless poor in it first 15-year of rule.
Over half the beneficiaries of land reforms belonged to lower Hindu castes and tribal groups.
When asked about the future of his communist government, Basu said: "It has a great future."
The marxists began a low-key celebration on Friday by a political meeting organised by the party in Calcutta and felicitation of Basu by his cabinet ministers.
The month-long celeberations will continue in Calcutta and other districts in the state, party officials said. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
